 Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Stewart is questionable for Monday’s game with an ankle injury. If he can’t play, Quinten Post could see more minutes off the bench, though he isn’t worth rostering in fantasy leagues. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart tallied 13 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings. 
 The Grizzlies gave Zach Edey the night off, so Beef Stew was inserted into the starting lineup. Stewart’s value was his defense and three-point shooting, but he played just 22 minutes. He missed most of the preseason with a sprained ankle, which likely factored into his playing time. Edey should be back for Monday’s game against the Jazz, which would push Stewart to the bench. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Isaiah Stewart will start Sunday’s game against the Kings. 
 While Coward returns after a one-game absence and pushes GG Jackson to the bench, the Grizzlies will not play Zach Edey due to injury management. As a result, Stewart will start at center in his second official game for the franchise. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Zach Edey (ankle) has been ruled out against the Kings on Sunday. 
 Edey will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back, which means he should be back to take on the Jazz on Monday. Expect Isaiah Stewart to start in his place, with Quinten Post filling out the backup minutes. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart notched four points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds and one steal in Friday’s win over the Warriors. 
 Stewart made his official Grizzlies debut on Friday, playing most of his minutes when starting center Zach Edey (8/10/3/1/2) was not on the floor. Unfortunately, Beef Stew picked up four fouls in the first half, including three in the first quarter, which limited him to 16 minutes. It remains to be seen what his role will look like once the ankle is no longer a concern, but Stewart isn’t someone worth rostering in most redraft leagues just yet.

 Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Stewart, injured during the preseason, did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz. Quinten Post logged 19 minutes off the bench as the backup center, and he’ll likely keep that role if Beef Stew can’t play on Friday. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Zach Edey with 6 points (3-of-5 FGs), 9 rebounds, and two blocks in 21 minutes. 
 The Grizzlies didn’t need Edey to play heavy minutes in this game to get the win. The Grizzlies have a couple of capable backup centers with Isaiah Stewart and Quentin Post. Given Edey’s injury history, it’s very possible that Edey doesn’t get heavy minutes this season, so the fantasy upside is more limited. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 The Grizzlies have a new frontcourt, with Boozer, the third overall pick in last summer’s draft, and Edey, returning from a season-ending ankle injury. They’ll play prominent roles in the Grizzlies’ lineup as the franchise rebuilds after trading Jaren Jackson Jr. and Ja Morant. Jerome and Coward also offer high fantasy upside with their starting roles.

 Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Stewart was initially doubtful for Wednesday’s season opener, so the downgrade in status is not a surprise. Quinten Post should slot in as the backup center behind starter Zach Edey.

 Nikola Jokić recorded 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Two nights after recording a triple-double in Denver’s comeback win over the Pelicans, Jokić posted a double-double on Monday. The three-time MVP finished with a complete stat line and committed one turnover, a good start to the week for those rostering him. However, the Nuggets are now 1-2, and they needed to erase a large deficit to get that lone win. Simply put, Jokić needs more help from teammates not named Jamal Murray. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandin Podziemski recorded 18 points (7-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Suns, Podziemski recorded his second 18-point game of the season. He played 33 minutes against the Nuggets, a positive sign given the back issue that kept Podz out of the Warriors’ October 21 season opener. Golden State has three more games in Week 2, ending with a Sunday/Monday back-to-back, so another injury management night could be on the horizon for Podziemski. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Stephen Curry accounted for 24 points (8-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 For just the second time in his illustrious career, Curry finished a game without missing a shot. After making his lone attempt during the first half, the Warriors guard shot 7-of-7 from the field in the second half as they pulled away from the Nuggets. Given Yaxel Lendeborg’s play, the Warriors didn’t have to rely as much on Curry. If that continues, it would make the future Hall of Fame guard’s job a little easier. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Player Stats

 Yaxel Lendeborg finished Monday’s win over the Nuggets with 31 points (9-of-19 FGs, 12-of-13 Fts), 12 rebounds, six assists, one block and one three-pointer.
 On a night when Stephen Curry attempted just one shot in the first half, Lendeborg had his best game as a pro. The rookie forward recorded his second double-double in four games and his first 30-point stat line. Given Lendeborg’s role with the Warriors and how much the team seems to trust him, he could be one of the best rookies in fantasy basketball this season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Mo Bamba started the second half and finished with 14 points (7-of-8 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and four blocks on Monday against the Grizzlies.
 Both Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (wrist) exited early from this game, which allowed Bamba and Josh Green to start the second half. Green wasn’t productive, but Bamba made the most of the opportunity. If Jackson remains out against the Spurs on Wednesday, Bamba may be in line to start. However, it is unlikely be produces to this level again, and the matchup against Victor Wembanyama isn’t ideal.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Ace Bailey recorded a double-double on Monday with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Grizzlies.
 Bailey has been excellent over Utah’s last two games, posting a double-double in both. However, his production could continue to climb. Lauri Markkanen (knee) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) both exited early from this game and could remain sidelined. Bailey already moved into the starting unit after opening night, but his usage will continue to increase if Utah is missing two starters. He’ll look to stay hot against the Spurs on Wednesday.

 Aaron Gordon was ejected from Monday’s game against the Warriors with 8:34 remaining in the fourth quarter. 
 Gordon was given two technical fouls in quick succession after arguing a call, ending his night with 8:34 left in the fourth quarter. He finished with seven points (2-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Marvin Bagley III replaced Gordon in the lineup after he was ejected.

 Keyonte George led the Jazz with 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), three rebounds and six assists in a 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies on Monday.
 It wasn’t enough to get the win, but George was the most productive scorer in this game. Both Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) exited early, which meant more offensive responsibility for George. If either, or both, misses time moving forward, George’s usage will continue to skyrocket. He has been excellent to start the year and will look to stay hot against the Spurs on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Ty Jerome

 Ty Jerome struggled on Monday but still contributed 15 points (4-of-15 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Jazz.
 After a scorching start to the season, Jerome fell back to earth in this game. His shot simply didn’t fall at the same rate, though he made up for it by dishing out a season high for assists. Jerome has been unreal to start the season, but it was never likely that he would maintain that pace. However, he should be a fantastic fantasy option for the rest of the season and one of the best value picks in fantasy basketball.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard

 Cedric Coward recorded a double-double on Monday with 16 points (6-of-12 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 110-105 win over the Jazz.
 Coward has gotten off to a strong start in his second season, especially over his last two games, where he has recorded a double-double in each. It was an ugly win, but Memphis is now 4-0 to start the season. Coward has been a big part of that and is currently a top-50 player in fantasy basketball. He’ll look to keep it going in Portland on Thursday.
 -  Noah Rubin
